name: What is the difference between partial pool demo and full pool removal?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between partial pool demolition and full pool removal for permit purposes?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between partial pool demolition and full pool removal for permit purposes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partial and full pool removal are not interchangeable. Partial demolition often means some of the shell remains underground, with specific openings, fill methods, and inspection steps to show the area will drain and stabilize. Full removal usually involves taking out more of the structure, which can create more hauling and possibly more site work, but it may simplify long-term site use. For permit purposes, the city cares about what remains in the ground and how the area is restored. The chosen method can change whether a soils report is needed, how the backfill is tested, and what final documentation is required. Homeowners should compare both options against their future plans for the yard or a future build.
acceptedAnswer.description: Partial pool demolition usually leaves part of the shell in place and may use fill materials to cover it, while full removal takes out more or all of the structure. Permit rules, inspections, and engineering requirements can be stricter for one method than the other.
